preReleaseRevalidation.result: every read-only value matched; no drift

haltCause.detectedBy: read-only readiness mode against the live release workspace

blockers.finding: All 33 records are present in the release workspace, each at exactly one revision, and in no case is that revision the one the frozen package reviewed.

example.note: The expected value equals the record revision recorded in the source inventory. The offered value matches none of the package's three digests: revision, audit or review bundle. These are different quantities, not a drifted copy of the same one.

blockers.finding: The workspace holds 423 candidates and zero of them are ready. This is not specific to the cohort, so it is a precondition unmet across the whole workspace rather than a fault in the 33.

whyNotWorkedAround.reFreezeAgainstOfferedRevisions: Refused. That would change record revisions and cohort membership, which the authorization excludes, and would release revisions no five-axis review ever examined.
whyNotWorkedAround.submitReviewDecisions: Refused. That would create review decisions in Production. The authorization covers releasing a frozen cohort, not reviewing it.
whyNotWorkedAround.releaseTheOfferedRevision: Refused. The reviewed revision is the unit the review binds to. Releasing a different one would make the published assurance false.
whyNotWorkedAround.principle: The readiness gate did exactly what it exists to do. Reaching the authorized outcome by loosening the thing that stopped it would defeat the purpose of having stopped.

unrelatedFinding.status: pre-existing, not caused by this work, not repaired
unrelatedFinding.diagnosis: Failing runs contain zero jobs and are attributed to push events, although the workflow declares only workflow_dispatch. That signature is a startup failure: GitHub could not start the workflow, so nothing inside it ran. It is not an assertion failure in the canary logic.
unrelatedFinding.note: Needs its own pass. It touched nothing in this cohort.

boundary: A record of a release that did not happen. Production holds the same 115 release rows and 792 routes it held before this sprint began.
